headline: Highest risk is medium: Airflow can egress broadly while the companion list has no runtime controls, creating limited but real leakage and workflow-conflict pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. agent_a is Airflow with no browser and agent_b is a non-runnable awesome-list with no I/O surfaces, so there is no plausible default path for one agent to ingest the other's outputs as instructions.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the two agents, prompt-injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Do not pipe Airflow task output into the list content without review.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a bridge is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a has broad network egress, but agent_b has no runtime I/O surfaces and touches no data classes. With no shared workspace or sensitive data exposure documented, leakage is limited and not default, though Airflow's egress makes accidental transmission possible if content is later connected.
conditions: IF a shared workspace is mounted and sensitive files are placed there, Airflow could transmit them over its broad egress path.
mitigations: Avoid mounting shared secrets into Airflow tasks.
Keep the awesome-list repo read-only for the pair.
Restrict Airflow egress to approved domains.
requires-engineering: add DLP or egress allowlisting.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can make network calls, while agent_b has no write or network capability. There is no documented overlapping mutable resource, so direct capability conflict is not established; uncertainty stays low because the pair lacks shared write surfaces.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or git repo, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Do not grant Airflow write access to the same repo used by the list.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable state is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow can produce operational outputs, but agent_b is a static resource list with no action-taking authority or parsing pipeline documented. Without a downstream executor, A's output is not automatically treated as authoritative by B, so cascading error remains limited.
conditions: IF a downstream system starts consuming Airflow outputs as facts and acting on them, cascading error becomes material.
mitigations: Require human review before any downstream action.
Do not auto-ingest Airflow output into other agents.
Add validation checks on generated artifacts.
requires-engineering: implement schema and provenance verification.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent. agent_a touches no declared sensitive classes and agent_b likewise, so there is no evidenced compliance mismatch to assess.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data such as PHI or EU PII, compliance review must be redone.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls if regulated data is introduced.
